senses.definition: To show someone something before committing to it, seeking their reaction rather than their approval. Softer than asking permission.
senses.caution: It implies you could proceed without them, which is why it works upward as courtesy and sideways as consultation. Said to someone whose sign-off you genuinely need, it can sound like you are minimising their role.
senses.example: Before I send this to the MD, can I run it by you?

cues.text: You have drafted a recommendation and want your manager's reaction before it goes further, without making it a formal approval request.
You are about to propose a change touching another team's system and want to show their lead first as a courtesy.
You are planning a surprise for your partner and want to check the idea with their sibling before booking anything.
You have chosen a restaurant for a group dinner and want to float it with one of them before committing everyone.

distractors: To hand a task over to whoever is better placed to do it than you are.
To circulate a finished document to a list of people and gather whatever comes back before the deadline.
To submit something formally for approval, so that nothing can move any further until the named person has signed it off.
To brief somebody thoroughly enough that they can take the questions on your behalf, because you will not be in the room when they get asked.
To test an idea against the numbers before anybody sees it, so that the version people do see has already survived the obvious objection. Nobody else is involved until it has.
